rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds and map the full retention window while keeping run time reasonable. This should reveal whether any peaks are unretained or still in the high-organic hold, guiding the next narrowing of phi window and adjustment of gradient steepness.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only improvement is to shorten t_last below 10 min. The observed peaks span roughly phi_e 0.11 to 0.59, so trimming the gradient window around that span and making it steeper should keep all compounds in-gradient while compressing the chromatogram.

We already have full resolution, so push retention down further to get the last peak under 10 min. A slightly higher phi1, shorter gradient, and higher temperature should move the late peak earlier while likely preserving enough margin on the closest pair.

The close 6/7 pair lost resolution when the run was made hotter and steeper, so back off both changes slightly while keeping t_last near 10 min. This tests whether that pair is strongly temperature-sensitive and should recover full resolution with only a modest time penalty.

The 6/7 pair is clearly very temperature-sensitive, with separation collapsing as T rises, while the same gradient window at 12 min and 40 C was fully resolved. Returning to 40 C but keeping the shorter 10 min gradient should test the shortest condition that still restores full resolution and may improve CRF over injection 2.

We have already reached the CRF maximum, so the only sensible follow-up is to probe the edge of failure and see whether an even faster method still preserves full resolution. This slightly steeper, shorter gradient should pull the last peak earlier while testing how much margin the critical 6/7 pair really has.

The 6/7 pair degrades when the gradient is made too steep or pushed to higher phi, so test whether narrowing the phi window while keeping the short 8 min gradient restores selectivity. This places the observed elution range more centrally in the gradient and may recover the critical pair without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak.

The 8 min, narrower window nearly restored the critical 6/7 pair, so a small reduction in slope should be enough to push it back above R=1.5 while likely keeping the last peak under 10 min. This targets a second max-CRF method with potentially shorter or more selective operation than the current optimum.

The optimum appears to be near the edge where the 6/7 pair just clears 1.5, so try lowering phi0 while keeping the successful tG, phi1, and T from injection 5. A lower starting strength should slightly shallow the effective gradient where the early-mid peaks elute and may improve the critical pair while keeping t_last under 10 min.

Lowering phi0 from 0.15 to 0.10 preserved CRF 1.000 while moving the critical 6/7 pair right to the resolution threshold, so one more step lower tests whether added early retention further stabilizes that pair without pushing t_last past 10 min. This maps the lower-phi0 edge of the optimum region.

Both 0.15/0.65/10/40 and 0.10/0.65/10/40 achieve CRF 1.000, so now test whether a slightly higher phi1 can shorten the run further while retaining enough selectivity at the lower phi0. This probes the upper-phi1 edge of the max-score region around the validated optimum.

The critical 6/7 pair worsens when phi1 is raised or phi0 is lowered, suggesting the optimum selectivity sits in a fairly narrow phi window. Testing a slightly higher phi0 with the successful phi1, tG, and T maps the other side of that window and checks whether a modestly narrower effective retention span can still keep CRF at 1.000.

Among the 10 min runs, lowering phi1 improved the critical 6/7 pair but cost some late retention, while lowering phi0 improved time but left the pair near threshold. Combining phi0 0.10 with phi1 0.60 should test whether a narrower, slightly lower-strength window gives a more comfortable selectivity margin while staying close to the 10 min t_last boundary.

The 10 min, 40 C optimum region is clearly bounded by the critical 6/7 pair, and we have not yet tested the diagonally opposite corner of the local space. Raising both phi0 and phi1 together keeps the window width at 0.50 but shifts the gradient to stronger solvent, which may preserve the pair better than raising phi1 alone while shortening the late elution.

At 10 min and 40 C, phi1 = 0.60 improved the critical pair while phi0 = 0.20 shortened the run, so combining those two favorable directions may land on another CRF 1.000 condition. This directly tests whether the 6/7 pair can stay above 1.5 with a shifted but narrower window and t_last still under 10 min.

Since 8 min at 40 C was too steep for the critical 6/7 pair, reduce temperature to strengthen retention and often improve selectivity while keeping the very short gradient. This tests whether a cooler run can recover full resolution and still keep the last peak within 10 min, potentially giving a faster max-score alternative.

Lowering temperature changed selectivity enough to create a new critical 5/6 pair, so give that cooler separation more gradient time rather than pushing temperature further. This isolates whether the 35 C selectivity can be useful if the slope is relaxed, while staying close to the proven successful phi window.

The temperature dependence is non-monotonic and strong, with the critical pair switching from 6/7 at 40 C to 5/6 at 35 C, so a further 5 C step will map whether a different selectivity regime appears. Keeping the proven phi window and tG fixed isolates temperature as the only variable and could reveal another fully resolved sub-10 min method.

The only major unexplored temperature near the high side is 55 C, and the data show temperature is the key driver of selectivity changes for the clustered mid peaks. This run maps the remaining hot-side behavior around the proven window, confirming whether the 50 C collapse of 6/7 continues monotonically or whether a different pair becomes limiting.

We already have two max-score methods, so use remaining injections to map a potentially faster robust region. Lower phi0 improved the critical pair at 40 C, while higher temperature shortens the run, so this combination tests whether added early retention can offset the hot/steep loss of selectivity and yield a short, fully resolved method.

The 10 min, 40 C max region is now well mapped, and the remaining unexplored adjacent point is a further increase of phi0 at fixed phi1. This checks whether the optimum boundary continues smoothly on the high-phi0 side or if early compression starts to erode the critical pair and/or produce near-unretained behavior.

With the core design space around 40 C already mapped and one hot-side point at 55 C nearly fully resolved, the only remaining informative adjacent temperature is 60 C. This completes the temperature series at the proven phi window and tG to define the upper-temperature selectivity limit.

We have max-CRF methods already, so the remaining value is robustness mapping around the proven optimum. Extending tG slightly at the best temperature and window will show how much safety margin can be gained on the critical 6/7 pair and quantify the time penalty near the optimum ridge.

With two injections left and the optimum already found, use one to probe a different ridge where lower phi0 helps the 6/7 pair while higher temperature shortens retention. A slightly longer gradient than the failed hot 8 min run may restore enough resolution to reveal whether a warm, lower-phi0 method can approach the optimum with extra speed margin.

Use the final injection to complete the temperature comparison for the second max-CRF window at phi0 0.10, phi1 0.65, tG 10. This isolates whether lowering temperature from the successful 40 C condition preserves the critical 6/7 pair or shifts the selectivity problem elsewhere in this alternate optimum region.
